chapter_note: A compact chapter with a clear two-part structure. ¶2-3 form a complete cosmological teaching pair: the summons (call) as a cosmic letter from Living Spirit to First Man, and the obedience (answer) as a cosmic letter from First Man to Living Spirit. Both cosmic beings and the letter metaphor stay entirely within the cosmic system. ¶4-6 then extend this 'letter' pattern to the institutional church — Light Mind as letter to the holy church, good works as letter to Christ. The editorial seam is sharp: the word 'also/too' in ¶4 explicitly extends the cosmic list, but the target is now the editor's community. Editorial fatigue data strongly confirms: substrate 12.50→0.98, institutional 0.00→16.09. The oldest teaching layer is the primordial call-and-answer narrative, which maps the summons and obedience as cosmic communications containing all foreknowledge.

paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: '[Once again he speaks to h]is disciples, preaching the word of life. And thus he speaks to them about' — pure formulaic attribution wrapping a substantive topic identification.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The topic identification names two cosmic entities — the summons (call) and the obedience (answer) — which are divinized beings in Manichaean cosmology (sixth sons of Living Spirit and First Man respectively). The naming of the teaching topic is substantive and defines the structure of what follows.

paragraphs.core_text: Consider the summons, which was sent from the Living Spirit in the beginning. He sent it to the First Man. It is a peace letter and greeting that he wrote and sent to his brother, in which all the tidings are written down, together with everything it will bring about and establish by that summons. That summons, the First Man [... is ordained to happen.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological narrative. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system: Living Spirit → First Man, summons → letter, cosmic tidings → foreknowledge. 'His brother' describes the cosmic kinship between Living Spirit and First Man. 'Consider' is pedagogical voice within the teaching tradition, not exhortation. 'In the beginning' anchors to cosmic time. The 'letter' metaphor describes what the summons IS as a cosmic communication — it does not reach outside the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The answer that was sent from the First Man came to the heights, to the Living Spirit. That is also a letter, which was sent from the First Man to the Living Spirit, in which all the tidings are written down; and every war and the struggles that he had waged. It did [...] in the answer that the First Man [... ...] everything that had happened and everything [that would happen], all that had been done and whatever is made ready to be done by him. The Living Spirit knew all the wars and the dangers and the contests that the rulers had waged against the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the cosmic pair: ¶2 described the summons (call downward, Living Spirit → First Man); ¶3 describes the obedience (answer upward, First Man → Living Spirit). Both sides remain cosmic: First Man, Living Spirit, the heights, the rulers, the wars. 'Everything that had happened and everything that would happen' — the letter contains cosmic foreknowledge, a substrate teaching about the nature of divine communication. The teaching unit is structurally complete after this paragraph.

Classic editorial seam. 'The Light Mind also... is a letter of peace too' — the word 'also/too' explicitly extends the cosmic letter pattern from ¶2-3, but now maps a cosmic entity (Light Mind) to a contemporary institution ('the holy church'). One side of the mapping reaches outside the cosmic system. 'The beloved Christ' uses devotional language. Institutional vocabulary score 14.08 confirms. The cosmic teaching was complete in ¶2-3; this paragraph applies it to the editor's community.

Continues the editorial extension. 'This light product, that shall be generated from the holy church' — maps the cosmic letter pattern to the church's collective good works. 'Fasting and prayers and good works' is fully institutional vocabulary (20.79 institutional score). 'Blessed Christ' is devotional. The paragraph is badly lacunose but the surviving text consistently applies the letter metaphor to church practice. Flagged by the pipeline as probable editorial extension.

Bridge connective 'Indeed, due to this' detected by pipeline. First-person address 'I say to you' pivots to audience. 'Everything that you will ask for will be given you' echoes NT promise language (cf. Matt 7:7, John 16:24). Devotional closure applying the letter teaching to the audience's prayer life. Despite heavy lacunae, the surviving fragments are entirely exhortatory.
